clue.text: Reveal secret light outside an Egyptian city

parts.note: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire or pipe

indicators.note: the city's name is placed around the little word an, which sits inside it

parts.note: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lets slip a secret about a lamp burning beyond an ancient Egyptian city.
explanation.walkthrough: A spill is a taper, easily missed as 'light'; Thebes was the ancient capital of Upper Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: To divulge something confidential is the idiom's whole meaning.

clue.text: Extend house in both directions to develop fully

explanation.surface: Building out on each side of a home lets it grow to its full size.
explanation.walkthrough: A house extended both ways literally gains a wing on each side; the idiom means to grow into one's full abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a young bird first flying, hence someone reaching full independence and potential; literally a house's wings spread out.

clue.text: One bargain that's unattainable

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a deal is an agreement or bargain

explanation.surface: A single bargain that is impossible to get hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect exists only in the imagination, so it can never actually be reached.

clue.text: An old soldier. I nearly go crazy

indicators.note: going crazy means these three words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A veteran fighter admits he is close to losing his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman foot soldier serving in a legion is a classic ancient warrior.

clue.text: Exhibit pet with a guilty look

parts.note: to hang a picture is to exhibit it in a gallery
a dog is a common household pet

explanation.surface: Someone shows off their animal, which looks ashamed of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamefaced, sheepish expression is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Money we pray for on a daily-basis

definitions.text: we pray for on a daily-basis

explanation.surface: Worshippers ask for cash every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lord's Prayer asks 'Give us this day our daily bread'; the word is also slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cash, and the staple food the Lord's Prayer requests each day.

clue.text: Artist, upset over alteration, left — Raphael, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a change is an alteration

explanation.surface: A painter, distressed by changes to his work, walks out, possibly Raphael himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Raphael the painter springs to mind as the artist, but here he is the angel of that name; 'upset' turns RA into AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael is one of the chief angels of scripture, an example of the rank.

clue.text: Out of its depth, here's a beast of burden

indicators.note: out means the letters are out of place and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal finds itself in water too deep for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges OF ITS DEPTH HERES, the 'of' of 'Out of its depth' being fodder, not part of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is nicknamed this as it carries loads across arid sands.

clue.text: Release without charging

explanation.surface: Letting someone go without pressing charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone, and costing nothing, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Sticky stuff, say, applied the wrong way to arm

parts.note: a gun is a firearm, a weapon or arm

indicators.note: the abbreviation is attached back to front, read from right to left

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Some gooey substance is put on someone's arm incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' standing for 'for example' (eg) is a common crossword convention; reversed by 'applied the wrong way' it makes GE.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for any unpleasant gooey or slimy matter.

clue.text: Swindle of £1.51?

parts.note: 151 pence: 151 is CLI in Roman numerals
the P for pence ends the sum

explanation.surface: Being cheated out of a pound and fifty-one pence.
explanation.walkthrough: £1.51 is 151p; 151 in Roman numerals is CLI, and p is the abbreviation for pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip someone is slang for overcharging or cheating them.

clue.text: Force both sides into a radio broadcast

indicators.note: the pair of letters is put inside the rearranged word
broadcast scatters the letters, as seed is broadcast

parts.note: left and right, abbreviated L and R

explanation.surface: Insisting that both parties appear on a wireless programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both sides' means left and right, not the outer letters of a word; 'broadcast' scrambles the fodder to RAIOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce someone into something hastily is to push it through like a train.

clue.text: Virago has to continue slowly

explanation.surface: A shrew of a woman must keep going at a crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' just joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, domineering woman is a fire-breathing monster; and to go on tediously is to drag on.

clue.text: Be guided by ruling and give up criminal activities

explanation.surface: Obeying a judgment and turning away from a life of crime.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruler draws a line to follow without deviation; a reformed crook is said to do the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Following a ruled line exactly, and becoming honest after a criminal life, are both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: Learner kept in beginning to adapt to rap over the knuckles

indicators.note: the learner's letter is held inside the longer phrase

parts.note: taking to something is starting to get used to it
L is the learner symbol on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee made to stay behind as they start adjusting to a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprimand or scolding, figuratively a smack on the hand.

clue.text: Prongs stuck into girl producing irritability

indicators.note: the prongs are pushed inside the girl's name

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name
tines are the prongs of a fork

explanation.surface: Poking a fork into a young woman would make anyone cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Short temper or peevishness.

clue.text: Punish all the spectators

explanation.surface: Disciplining the entire crowd at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: At British schools and universities, to gate a pupil is to confine them to grounds as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Confining a student to college is a punishment; the attendance at a match is its crowd count.

clue.text: Close main line

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open ocean

explanation.surface: Shutting down the principal railway route.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten or shut something tight.

clue.text: Emphatic pronoun with which fairies end letter?

explanation.surface: Grammar point about how sprites sign off their correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter from the fairies might sign off 'Yours, Elves'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflexive pronoun used for emphasis, as in 'do it yourselves'; and a sign-off split into two words.

clue.text: Do without female's soothing words

indicators.note: the female letter is left out of the longer word

parts.note: a do is a party, a social function
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Managing without a woman's comforting speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb but is a noun: a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction is a smooth, ingratiating manner of speaking, like an anointing balm.

clue.text: Hanging out, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that we want a word spoken aloud like another

parts.note: out means away, absent

explanation.surface: Being suspended outside, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: An anchor aweigh has just left the seabed and hangs from the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor raised clear of the bottom is suspended in the water.

clue.text: First sections of Handel piece needed practice

indicators.note: the opening part of the composer's name is taken

parts.note: a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Playing the opening movements of a Handel work requires rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a settled custom or practice.

clue.text: Doctor in South American country gets new issue

indicators.note: the doctor goes inside the country's name

parts.note: Chile is a country of South America

explanation.surface: A medic working in Chile receives a fresh supply of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for offspring or descendants.

clue.text: Duck a trick

explanation.surface: Someone ducks a con.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade by moving aside, and a cunning ruse, are both senses.

clue.text: 'Reverse arms" well ordered

indicators.note: reverse tells us to turn the next word back to front

parts.note: guns are arms, weapons

explanation.surface: A military drill command, carried out with precision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse arms' is a real drill order, but 'Reverse' turns GUNS into SNUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug can mean neat and tidy, compact and shipshape.

clue.text: Tablecloth with indentations, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this says the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: bays are indentations in a coastline

explanation.surface: A table covering with dents in it, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Baize is the green woollen cloth covering billiard and card tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Baize is the felt-like fabric used to cover snooker and card tables.

clue.text: Judge takes some outside employment

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A magistrate takes on a second job outside court.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Judge takes' does not fit a verb meaning judge; 'takes' is a link word, so the definition is just 'Judge'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to consider or form an opinion.

clue.text: Steward's on the fiddle — that's succinct

indicators.note: a fiddle is a swindle or a tinkering, so these letters are fiddled into new order

explanation.surface: A steward is caught swindling, and that is the brief version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' looks like the indicator phrase, but ON and THE are fodder: 'fiddle' rearranges STEWARDS ON THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief and pleasantly to the point is the idiom's meaning.
